Arca only opens files that the system hands over (content or file addresses).

Choose a document. Arca inspects it inside an isolated sandbox that has no access to your files, network or other apps, shows what is hidden in it, and displays a safe preview as plain text. Nothing in the document is ever run.
You can also drop a file onto this window or share it to Arca from another app.
This app has no network permission. Documents never leave your device.
Arca is free software made by people who ask for nothing in return but support. See who they are and how to help.

Checking this file exceeded its time limit. A file that is built to waste time is itself a sign of attack. It was stopped and nothing was opened.
The file is damaged or built in a way that no honest program produces. It was refused before any of it was interpreted.
Arca does not know how to read this kind of file, so it shows nothing from it. The file has not been opened or run.
The content is protected by a password, so it cannot be inspected without it. Arca asks for a password only to open the file inside its sandbox; it never keeps it and never tries to guess it.
The password does not open this document. Nothing was opened.
If you know the password, Arca opens the file inside its sandbox and checks what is in it. The password is used once, kept only in memory and wiped when you close the document.

Arca rebuilds the document from its safe parts only and checks the result again. The copy opens in any program without macros, remote content or other active parts.
Macros and scripts, embedded and linked objects, ActiveX, remote templates and images, links that load by themselves, data connections, DDE and risky formulas, and anything the container hides.

All metadata (where and when it was taken, the camera and its serial number, the author), the embedded thumbnail, colour profile and comments, every frame of an animation but the first, and anything stored after the picture.

The copy is a new PNG written from the picture’s pixels alone, so nothing of the original file’s structure survives. A photograph can become larger than its JPEG, a picture of more than 4 megapixels is reduced (unless you keep the full size), an animation keeps only its first frame, and colours are shown as sRGB.

A PDF is rebuilt from its pages: text, pictures and fonts stay exactly as they are. Bookmarks, links, attachments, forms, signatures and old revisions do not; the look of form fields and stamps stays as part of the page.

The copy is a new .docx, .xlsx or .pptx written from the text, tables and pictures the viewer shows: macros, embedded objects, fields, forms and the old file’s hidden data have nowhere to come from. Complex layout (columns, floating shapes, charts) is simplified.
Embedded objects (including charts), thumbnails and signatures are removed from OpenDocument files.
Names, company, paths, printer and editing history.
Hidden data blocks that other programs attach to the document.
Off: a picture of more than 4 megapixels is reduced (a 12-megapixel photo becomes 3), which takes seconds. On: up to 16 megapixels are kept, which takes minutes on a phone.
Remarks of reviewers. The text of the document is not changed.
Deleted text disappears and inserted text becomes normal text. This changes the document.
The original file is never changed. The copy is saved only where you choose.
